summary: Ran the one-off configs/accounts.yml -> DB migration for real (previously blocked on a password for the new User row). Created 1 User, 2 Strategy rows (S007/CTRADER, S009/BYBIT), 2 Account rows (CTRADER demo, BYBIT mainnet), and 2 AccountStrategy links with initial_balance seeded from accounts.yml. APP_SECRET_KEY must be exported from .env manually before running this script -- it does not load .env itself, same as the rest of webapp/.

Installed and loaded the S009 launchd scheduler (com.algo.s009-paper), which had never actually been running: no plist under ~/Library/LaunchAgents, no launchd job, no cron entry -- since the last manual run on 2026-08-06 the paper ledger/state had gone stale (last_day stuck at 2026-08-05) while 4 real positions sat open on the dedicated Bybit-algo009 mainnet account with nothing auto-rebalancing them. Fixed a real bug this exposed in scripts/s009_tick.py: tick() defaulted its now parameter to timezone-aware UTC (datetime.now(timezone.utc)), but utils/trade_logger.py writes event timestamp fields as naive local time, so _has_event_today's since-cutoff comparison raised "can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes" on every idle tick once a heartbeat had already been logged for the day -- same failure signature as the two "S009 cycle subprocess exited non-zero" entries already in S009.log from 2026-08-03. Changed the default to naive local time (matching the logger and scripts/s007_tick.py's own default); this now parameter only affects heartbeat dedup/log-file day-naming, not the actual UTC trading-day boundary (_expected_last_closed_day() is independent of it). Added tests/scripts/test_s009_tick.py (regression test replays the exact two-consecutive-idle-ticks crash, plus branch coverage for the needs-cycle/timeout/nonzero-exit/state-did-not-advance paths, mirroring tests/scripts/test_s007_tick.py's structure). Per explicit user confirmation, also switched deployment/com.algo.s009-paper.plist from --broker off (shadow-only) to --broker execute --allow-mainnet, so the scheduler now auto-rebalances the real mainnet book daily; verified via BybitExec.positions()/wallet_equity() (read-only) that the reload itself placed no orders.

Replaced the S007-specific Ofelia job-run label with one generic, permanent dispatcher job (docker-compose.yml's 'dispatch' job runs scripts/scheduler_tick.py every minute). The dispatcher reads deployment/schedule.yml (strategies[].schedule / tasks[].command+schedule, 5-field cron matched via croniter) and subprocess-invokes `webapp.runner --strategy <name>` or a task's command when due -- adding a strategy's cadence or a background job is now a schedule.yml edit + code review, never a docker-compose.yml change. Deliberately config-file-based, not a DB table: a task always references a script that has to be written anyway, so a DB row would not actually enable 'add without redeploy'. Verified end-to-end on Podman: image rebuilds with croniter, a simulated in-window Monday timestamp correctly triggered a real S007 cycle through the container (log + account_strategies.last_cycle_at both updated), and Ofelia registers/fires the new job. Found and fixed a real doc/image mismatch along the way: the actual pulled mcuadros/ofelia:latest fires a 5-field '* * * * *' schedule EVERY SECOND, not every minute, contradicting its own README's 'seconds optional in 0.4.x+' claim -- Ofelia's own outer schedule needed the 6-field seconds-first form ('0 * * * * *'); this is separate from and does not affect schedule.yml's 5-field croniter strings, which are a different parser entirely.

Found and fixed a serious live incident: the Podman machine VM (hosting the Ofelia scheduler container since yesterday's S007 cutover) does not reliably resume its internal clock after the host Mac wakes from sleep. Its clock froze at 2026-08-09 14:07 (last real firing) and stayed 18+ hours behind while `podman ps`/`podman machine inspect` both kept reporting it healthy/running -- Ofelia's cron scheduler silently stopped firing S007/S009 dispatch with zero errors anywhere. This meant S007 had NO live coverage at all overnight (legacy launchd unloaded yesterday, new Docker path silently dead) until caught this morning before the 10:00 Kyiv session. `chronyc makestep` / restarting chronyd inside the VM did not fix it -- only a full `podman machine stop` + `start` resynced the clock. Fix: scripts/podman_healthcheck.py, installed as a launchd job (deployment/com.algo.podman-healthcheck.plist, every 5 min via StartCalendarInterval) -- launchd supervises the Docker/Podman layer from OUTSIDE it, since launchd is the one layer already proven immune to this Mac's sleep/wake cycles. Compares host vs VM epoch; beyond a 120s threshold, restarts the machine + `docker compose up -d ofelia` and verifies the fix took. Caught and fixed a real bug in the fix itself before trusting it: subprocess.run(['podman', ...]) failed silently under launchd's minimal PATH (no /opt/podman/bin), misreported as 'machine unreachable' -- switched to the absolute binary path. Verified live: detected a real 207s drift immediately after the manual machine restart and self-healed correctly; a second run confirmed the fixed PATH issue with a clean, quiet (healthy) exit. 6 new tests, full suite (78) green. Per user decision: S009's DB-driven path stays broker='off' (deferred) until this reliability gap was closed -- this incident is exactly why that caution was right.

Fixed two real bugs found live during S007 first trading day on the new Docker/Ofelia path: (1) dispatch job-run container ran in UTC instead of Europe/Kyiv (missing TZ env on the label), causing S007 to silently skip its 10:00-13:00 Kyiv session window; (2) scheduler_tick had no overlap guard, so a slow cycle (55-118s, observed live) let two dispatch ticks run the same strategy concurrently -- added a per-(kind,name) file lock under data/.scheduler_locks with stale-lock self-healing. Also fixed podman_healthcheck.py: the watchdog previously treated a fully-unreachable (stopped) machine as non-healable and did nothing, leaving zero dispatch coverage for 25+ minutes live during an open real position; now both drift and unreachable trigger the same heal path, and each heal step is wrapped so a failing subprocess call cannot crash the healthcheck itself. Root cause of the recurring Podman-machine instability (3 outages in ~2.5h today) remains unexplained -- watchdog now reacts correctly to all observed failure modes but does not fix why the VM keeps dying.
